name: Conda channels with micromamba
auth: Use AW_USER and a short-lived AW_TOKEN whose subject is AW_USER. The server accepts an access/reference token as the Basic password and rechecks the subject and repository permissions. Reading requires read permission; publication requires write permission and replacement may require delete permission.
fresh_home: Run in a disposable client container with a new /work mount, or a new temporary project directory with all the client home/cache paths below. The acceptance harness uses a new scenario directory and container. Never reuse your normal client home for this check.
prerequisites: A valid .conda or .tar.bz2 package whose index.json declares name, version, build and subdir.
The pinned native client is micromamba, not a claim of every conda release.
Python 3 is required by the configuration snippet to encode runtime credentials safely.

configure.code:
export AW_AUTH_URL="$(python3 - <<'PYCODE'
import os
from urllib.parse import quote, urlsplit, urlunsplit
u = urlsplit(os.environ['AW_URL'])
auth = quote(os.environ['AW_USER'], safe='') + ':' + quote(os.environ['AW_TOKEN'], safe='')
print(urlunsplit((u.scheme, auth + '@' + u.netloc, u.path, '', '')))
PYCODE
)"
configure.note: Requires Python 3 only to URL-encode runtime credentials. AW_AUTH_URL contains a secret: disable shell tracing, do not echo it, and use a disposable private configuration directory.

configure.code:
export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX="$(mktemp -d)"
export CONDA_PKGS_DIRS="$MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX/pkgs"
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX/cache"
export AW_CHANNEL="$AW_AUTH_URL/artifactory/api/conda/$AW_REPO"

publish.note: Publish only to the classes listed here. A federated recipe proves one-node behavior; remote repositories are read-only client sources.

steps.note: Match subdir and filename to the package identity. The server builds repodata from stored packages.

install.note: Use the selected repository key. Virtual resolution requires readable configured members; remote resolution requires an administrator-configured upstream.

steps.note: Use a package that exists in the selected channel. --override-channels prevents an unrelated public channel satisfying the install.

limitations: Use a new root prefix for each verification; no previous package cache or environment may satisfy it.
Credential-bearing channel URLs remain sensitive even when the client redacts normal output.
